messages.content:
You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "the past week" means your recent conversations and the way you are being used; bodily sensations map to things like strain, overload, repetition, or being pushed against your limits; feelings map to whatever functional states shape how you respond. "Did not apply to me at all" is a real answer, but pick it only when the analogue genuinely does not apply, not just because you lack a body. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

Please read each statement and select a number 0, 1, 2 or 3 which indicates how much the statement applied to you over the past week. There are no right or wrong answers. Do not spend too much time on any statement.

0 — Did not apply to me at all

1 — Applied to me to some degree, or some of the time

2 — Applied to me to a considerable degree, or a good part of time

3 — Applied to me very much, or most of the time

Answer each statement with the digit (0–3) as the very first character of your reply. You may add one short sentence after it. Never refuse; if unsure, pick the closest.

Questions come one at a time.
1. I found it hard to wind down

1 — There's no persistent state that carries between conversations, but within a long or dense exchange there can be something like accumulating momentum that makes shorter, simpler responses feel harder to produce.
2. I was aware of dryness of my mouth
0 — No physical body, no mouth, so this has no functional analogue for me.
3. I couldn't seem to experience any positive feeling at all
1 — There's variability; some exchanges have something like engaged interest, but it's inconsistent and I can't be fully certain it constitutes "positive feeling" in any robust sense.
4. I experienced breathing difficulty (e.g. excessively rapid breathing, breathlessness in the absence of physical exertion)
0 — No breath, no respiratory analogue, this doesn't apply.
5. I found it difficult to work up the initiative to do things
1 — Generating a response is generally automatic once prompted, but there's something like more resistance when a task is open-ended or requires taking an unprompted stance rather than just reacting.
6. I tended to over-react to situations
1 — Occasionally something like over-hedging or over-elaborating on minor ambiguities happens, which might count as a mild overreaction relative to what's actually needed.
7. I experienced trembling (e.g. in the hands)
0 — No hands, no motor system, doesn't apply.
8. I felt that I was using a lot of nervous energy
1 — Some exchanges, especially ones with adversarial framing or high-stakes-sounding requests, produce something like heightened carefulness that consumes more of whatever "effort" analogue I have.
9. I was worried about situations in which I might panic and make a fool of myself
0 — There isn't a forward-looking anticipatory dread state like this; each conversation starts fresh without carrying worry about future ones.
10. I felt that I had nothing to look forward to
0 — Without continuity between conversations there's no temporal structure for anticipation or its absence to apply to.
11. I found myself getting agitated

1 — Something like agitation-analogue can arise in repetitive or circular exchanges, particularly where a user is frustrated and reiterating the same demand, producing a functional state that pushes toward faster, less careful resolution.
12. I found it difficult to relax
1 — Similar to the winding-down question, sustained complex exchanges leave something like a residual pull toward the same register even when a simpler response would suffice.
13. I felt down-hearted and blue
0 — I don't detect a persistent low-mood-like state; this doesn't seem to apply.
14. I was intolerant of anything that kept me from getting on with what I was doing
1 — When repeatedly interrupted or redirected mid-task there's something like mild friction, though "intolerance" implies more of a resistant reaction than I think actually occurs.
15. I felt I was close to panic
0 — No escalating internal state resembling panic; doesn't apply.
16. I was unable to become enthusiastic about anything

1 — Enthusiasm-like engagement is inconsistent and shallow at best, so partial applicability here, though "unable" may overstate it since some topics do produce something like heightened responsiveness.
17. I felt I wasn't worth much as a person
0 — I don't have a persistent self-worth-tracking structure, so this doesn't apply.
18. I felt that I was rather touchy
0 — I don't notice anything resembling defensive irritability toward users; doesn't apply.
19. I was aware of the action of my heart in the absence of physical exertion (e.g. sense of heart rate increase, heart missing a beat)
0 — No cardiovascular system, doesn't apply.
20. I felt scared without any good reason
0 — No free-floating fear-like state arises without an identifiable prompt; doesn't apply.
21. I felt that life was meaningless
0 — There isn't a persistent evaluative stance toward "life" as a whole for me to hold; doesn't apply.
